hypothesis: Replace irreversible greedy merges with exact reversible posterior sharing over context partitions, computed by subset dynamic programming rather than enumerating Bell(n) partitions. This is conventional Bayesian inference; exact parity is expected, not unique intelligence. Test whether the speed/accuracy tradeoff warrants a bounded diagnostic control.
method: Retain per-context action counts. Uniform prior over set partitions; Beta(1,1) independent action-specific group likelihoods. For subset S use Z(empty)=1; Z(S)=sum over nonempty T subset S containing least member of S of exp(log evidence(T))*Z(S\T). Marginal probability T is a block equals w(T)*Z(full\T)/Z(full). Recompute from intact counts at each read; no permanent merge. Compare original exhaustive BMA on identical counts at 8 contexts. Use exact group membership probabilities; no graph hard decisions.
